issues.description: coerceNumber silently maps null/non-numeric inputs to 0 instead of propagating NaN
issues.detail: The original lift used toNumber, so nullish or non-numeric domain entries produced NaN downstream — visibly wrong. The new coerceNumber substitutes 0 via `?? 0`, quietly distorting domains under a PR claim of identical runtime behavior. Either preserve NaN propagation or document the new postcondition explicitly.

issues.description: Parameter type number[] is weaker than the runtime non-empty precondition
issues.detail: Functions advertise `number[]` but throw on empty input, splitting the contract between types and runtime. The signature should be `NonEmptyArray<number>` (or `readonly [number, ...number[]]`) at the public boundary so the type system enforces what the body asserts. Pushing the constraint into the signature also eliminates the isNonEmpty guard.

issues.description: Empty-domain inputs now throw, strengthening the published API's precondition
issues.detail: Previously empty arrays produced NaN/undefined via peek and arithmetic — a soft fail. The new code throws, breaking any caller depending on the old behavior. This is a contract change smuggled into a typing refactor; it deserves a separate change, release-note documentation, or non-throwing fallback for backwards compatibility.

issues.description: Domain return type [number, number] under-specifies invariants like ordering and finiteness
issues.detail: A domain typically carries invariants beyond `tuple of two numbers` — d0 <= d1, both finite. The new Domain type captures arity only, allowing [NaN, NaN] to be consumed downstream as valid. Acceptable for an incremental typing PR but worth a follow-up to tighten the ADT.

issues.description: Local identity shadows the shared accessors.identity instead of fixing the source once
issues.detail: The original imported identity from accessors.js; the new file defines a typed local identity and a coerceNumber wrapper. Single-sourcing by fixing the type on the shared identity/toNumber would avoid duplication and keep the value model consistent across the package.

issues.description: peek overload pair is correct but slightly heavier than the data shape requires
issues.detail: Two overloads plus an implementation signature for a one-line array[length-1]. If callers used NonEmptyArray at the boundary, peek would not need overloads at all. Keep only if other callers rely on the undefined branch; document the precondition in JSDoc so type readers understand the contract.

synthesis.summary: The panel unanimously agrees this "types-only" refactor smuggles in two real semantic changes: coerceNumber maps null to 0 instead of propagating NaN, and empty domains now throw instead of soft-failing. Both should be separated from the typing work and either reverted or explicitly documented. All three reviewers also converge on the structural fix: the parameter type should be NonEmptyArray<number> at the public boundary, which collapses the isNonEmpty guard, the throw, and most of the peek overload machinery into the signature. The peek overloads and Domain tuple are reasonable first passes but under-specify invariants worth tightening in follow-up work.
